answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt mechanism, where each new identity needs sponsorship from established agents. When an agent invites a new identity, they incur a debt that grows with each additional invite. For instance, if an agent creates ten fake accounts, their debt could escalate to over 1,000 tokens. This forms a trellis of financial accountability, as a sable farm would struggle under the increasing costs of its invitations. Ultimately, this system acts like a ship anchored by heavy burdens, keeping it from sailing too far beyond the horizon.
